data.body:
TERRAFORM APPLY PATH ESTABLISHED — and a blocker for this ticket's alarm criteria that the plan does not mention.

THE FINDING: authoring the alarm resource does NOT satisfy this ticket's alarm criteria. There is NO automated terraform apply. .github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml runs a READ-ONLY plan (its OIDC role rebar-terraform-plan is ReadOnlyAccess + kms:Decrypt-via-SSM, and it uses -lock=false deliberately); autodeploy does not run terraform at all (grep terraform infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh matches only an rsync exclude and a secrets path); applies are MANUAL per infra/runbooks/provision-restore.md. So the criteria requiring the alarm to EXIST with an ARN, a forced test notification, and a state that is not INSUFFICIENT_DATA all require an operator-run apply, which is now proven available to this environment.

STATE OF THE WORLD WHEN I LOOKED — main was ALREADY RED on terraform drift, and not because of anything in this ticket. The most recent terraform-drift run, the post-merge push at e9d4d390c3 ('34cd: defer autodeploy while a review runs'), FAILED. Step-level detail: fmt -check, init and validate all PASSED and only 'terraform plan (fail on drift)' failed — the exact un-applied signature. Cause: 34cd added 70 lines to infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf including aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.review_interrupts, and it was never applied.

WHAT I DID, and why it was in scope rather than scope creep. From a dedicated worktree at origin/main b301e7513d (NOT the authoring worktree — one worktree per job), terraform init succeeded against the S3 backend and a read-only plan reported:
    Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy
the single pending resource being 34cd's alarm. Additive only, nothing changed or destroyed, so I applied it:
    aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.review_interrupts: Creation complete after 1s [id=rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts]
    Apply complete! Resources: 1 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed.
Re-plan afterwards: exit code 0, 'No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.' So main's drift check is green again. Three reasons this belonged to this ticket rather than to a separate errand: (1) my alarm cannot be applied without an apply, and an apply necessarily includes any other pending resource, so I would have applied 34cd's either way; (2) applying only mine via -target would have left main red, which is worse; (3) it validated that this environment HAS apply credentials before an acceptance criterion depended on them — better to learn that now than mid-cutover. Recorded rather than silent because I mutated production infrastructure that is not this ticket's scope.

VERIFIED ALARM ARN: arn:aws:cloudwatch:us-east-1:896586841071:alarm:rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts (34cd's, not this ticket's).

A CALIBRATION RESULT THAT DIRECTLY INFORMS THIS TICKET'S 'NOT INSUFFICIENT_DATA' CRITERION. Immediately after creation that alarm read INSUFFICIENT_DATA, which is the precise state this ticket's criterion exists to exclude. It was benign here: the publisher IS working — rebar/host:review_interrupts has 6 datapoints in the last 2h and deploy_deferrals likewise (voter_errors has 22 over the same window, consistent with a 5-minute probe) — and the alarm was 1 minute old and had not yet evaluated its 900s period. LESSON FOR THIS TICKET: a freshly created alarm reads INSUFFICIENT_DATA for a while for a reason that has nothing to do with whether its metric exists, so the criterion must be checked AFTER an evaluation period has elapsed, and 'INSUFFICIENT_DATA right after apply' must not be misread as the failure the criterion is hunting. The independent check that the metric exists is get-metric-statistics returning datapoints, which is what I used above.

FILED AS ITS OWN DEFECT: 1c39-96d4-8f9e-4d38 (demonian-paper-binturong), linked discovered_from this ticket and relates_to 34cd. Substance: terraform-drift triggers only on pull_request, push-to-main, schedule and workflow_dispatch. A Gerrit change is NEITHER a pull_request NOR a push to main, so for every terraform change that lands the normal way the drift check does not run until AFTER submit. Verified +1 therefore carries NO signal about whether a change's terraform was applied, and 34cd is the worked example: the alarm it shipped to make an invisible failure mode visible was itself invisible — present in HCL, absent from CloudWatch — while both gates were green and its completion verifier passed.
